name: Cross-Stitch Sampler
summary: The whole game is a living cross-stitch sampler on Aida cloth: every cell is a real thread X, contours are backstitched.
description: The world is a piece of beige Aida fabric with visible holes. Everything that is not bare cloth is embroidered on a 3.2-unit stitch grid: characters and props are small cell grids where each cell is a two-stroke thread cross with shadow, sheen and ply twist, outlined with a dark backstitch. Flowers are French knots, water is satin stitch, pickups are glass beads and buttons, and enemies are stitched into existence by a needle and unravel into loose threads when they die. It reads like grandma's Halloween sampler come to life: warm, cosy and tactile.
bestFor: puzzle and board-like games on a grid
avoidFor: smooth free-form animation and rotation of characters
high-detail portraits or large bosses with fine features

difficulty.why: Works like pixel art on a coarse grid – new motifs are simple stitch patterns.

technique.resolution: Native resolution with smoothing on. Motifs are baked at 8 sprite px per stitch cell (cell = 3.2 world units, so 2.5 px per unit) and drawn scaled; positions snap to the 3.2-unit stitch grid, not to screen pixels.
technique.summary: Every visible colour cell is a pre-rendered thread X (3 jittered variants per colour) blitted on a world-aligned 3.2-unit grid over a procedural Aida fabric texture; outlines are 4-pass backstitch strokes along cell edges. Large ground areas are merged into per-colour Path2D runs filled with seamless 4x4-stitch patterns.
technique.linework: Backstitch only: straight thread segments along cell edges, shortened by a small gap at each hole, drawn in 4 passes (shadow rgba(35,20,10,0.36) at w*1.12 offset (+0.28w,+0.42w); dark body colour*0.72 at w; body colour at w*0.62; sheen mix(colour, white, 0.45) alpha 0.7 at w*0.26). Character outline = #2b1d1d at 2.2 sprite px (0.88 world units); inner contours 1.7 px; ground region borders 1.0 world unit. Round caps.
technique.shading: Cell-quantised: form shading is chosen per cell from 3-4 thread ramps (e.g. pumpkin Q/q/O/o, leaves G/g/l/L) using a sphere normal lit from the upper left (l = -0.5nx - 0.6ny + 0.62nz) plus 4x4 Bayer jitter. Within each stitch: dark underside (colour*0.7), top ply, white sheen line and twist ticks give the thread volume.
technique.lighting: Soft warm light from the upper left baked into each stitch (shadow offset +0.45/+0.85 px down-right) and into motif drop shadows (blurred #28160c, alpha 0.42, offset 1.4/2.4 px). Additive warm candle glows: a light pool around the hero, a flickering face glow, gem and lantern glows. Brown radial vignette; a multiply #2a2050 night tint up to 16% as the run progresses.
technique.texture: Aida cloth everywhere: 8 px hole grid with hole corners at 0.74 brightness, hole edges 0.93, a 2x2 weave checker (1.03 / 0.985), row and column slub noise, plus faint long slub threads; large soft fold highlights and shadows (max 15% alpha) over the ground.

palette.name: Backstitch black
palette.role: Outline thread for characters and most props

palette.role: Trunks, roots, path border, feet (#45291c dark, #c79a66 light)

palette.role: Enemy faces, seeds, light rings (#d8bc7f shade, #fbf8f0 white)

palette.role: Fast spirit enemy (#97b6d4 shade, #3c5078 outline and eyes)

palette.name: Cardinal red
palette.role: Scarf, heart, mushrooms, crits (#7a1c24 dark, #e65f3e light)

palette.name: Ochre field
palette.role: Crop rows, autumn trees (#a6782e, #e3b24d gold, #f2d37c light)

paletteRules: Every colour is a named thread (single-letter code). Use only these threads; shading never invents in-between colours, it switches to the next thread of the ramp.
Stitch rendering derives exactly four tones from each thread: colour*0.64 underlay, colour*0.7 underside, colour, mix(colour, white, 0.5) sheen. Hit flash = mix(colour, white, 0.6).
Bare Aida cloth stays the dominant colour (about half of the screen); meadow is only sparsely stitched (3–40% of cells) so the fabric shows through.
Shadows are always warm brown rgba(40,22,10,a), never black or grey.
Each actor type owns one hue family (hero orange + navy, small enemy purple + cream, fast enemy pale blue, brute purple-brown) so a crowd stays readable.
No neon, no pure black fills, no gradients inside stitched areas; gradients only on beads, buttons, knots, sequins and glows.

typography.role: Numbers, titles, card names, timer – chunky rounded hand-made display face
typography.css: font: 900 35px/1 'Grandstander', sans-serif; letter-spacing: 1px; color: #a3302a; text-shadow: 0 1px 0 rgba(255,250,235,.9), 0 2px 0 rgba(90,30,15,.25);

typography.role: Body text, labels, descriptions, hints – friendly handwriting

background.summary: An infinite piece of Aida cloth. Noise fields classify every 3.2-unit cell into meadow, forest, field, pond or path; each material is embroidered differently, and every region border is backstitched. Baked per 256-unit chunk.
layers: Aida fabric pattern (16x16-hole tile, 8 px per hole, scaled to 0.4 units per px) over the whole chunk
Path cells: no stitches, lightened with rgba(255,250,236,0.42) – bare linen

Fill stitches merged into per-colour row runs: sparse meadow greens (L/l/g, dithered density), dense rust forest (z/X/x with rare gold and orange accents), half-stitch crop rows in fields (every 4th row left empty)
Pond as satin stitch: blocks of up to 3 cells in a brick pattern, 4 depth tones W/u/n/N
Decals on a 21-unit jittered grid: French-knot flower clusters with stems, lazy-daisy flowers, three-stitch grass tufts, sequins, bead rows, mushrooms, leaf motifs, lily pads, water ripple threads
Backstitched region contours, 1.0 unit thread: navy #2b4b70 around ponds, brown #7c4a2b along paths, dark brown #45291c elsewhere
Cloth light: low-res overlay of soft diagonal folds (warm white vs brown, max 15% alpha)

characters.summary: Characters are tiny cell grids (hero 9x11 cells = 28.8x35.2 units) written as strings of thread codes. Each is baked into a sprite: blurred drop shadow, dark thread underlay, one cross stitch per cell, a #2b1d1d backstitch outline around the silhouette, optional inner backstitch contours and free backstitch segments for details (stems, mouths, brows). 3 frames, mirrored for left, plus a white-flash copy.
rules: Design on the cell grid only: 7–9 cells wide for small actors, ~15x17 for a brute. One letter = one stitch.
Always outline the silhouette with a dark backstitch (2.2 sprite px); add an inner contour where two bright areas meet (hero face uses #6c2817 around the yellow carving).
Big readable faces: 1-cell eyes, 1-row mouths in yellow/cream on a darker field; fine lines (mouths, brows) are backstitch segments, not stitches.
Animate by swapping only the bottom row (legs) or top row (leaves/tail) between 3 frames; the body block never moves.
Snap the sprite origin to the world stitch grid (gx = round(x/3.2 - w/2), gy = round(y/3.2) - h) so actors move in whole stitches.
Spawn = progressive stitching (6 partial masks, bottom-up), death = the same in reverse plus thread snippets – never fade or scale a motif.

effects.name: Projectile seed
effects.how: A cream seed (gradient #fffaf0 to #c9a86a, outline #8a6a3a) with a 3-dash running-stitch trail in warm yellow, rotated to the flight direction; 14x5 world units.

effects.name: Hit
effects.how: A cream French knot pops for 0.18 s at the enemy's top plus, with 60% chance, one curly loose-thread snippet in the enemy's colours flung upward under gravity; the enemy sprite gets an overlaid white-flash copy.

effects.name: Death unravel
effects.how: The enemy un-stitches through the 6 partial masks, 7 (brute: 16) curly thread snippets in its palette fly out with gravity 150 and spin, 1–5 glass beads bounce, a brute drops a sewing button, and a dashed thread ring (dash 1.6/1.2, width 0.9) expands from 3 to 11 units.

effects.name: Spawn needle
effects.how: While an enemy is being stitched in, a silver needle (gradient #8c8f96 to #f4f6fa) with red thread darts left and right across the motif at the current stitching row.

effects.name: Pickups
effects.how: Small XP = orange glass bead #f39a2e (5.4 units) with additive glow and 0.8-unit bob; big XP = gold four-hole sewing button #e3b24d (9 units) with cross thread, gently rocking. Collect = tiny cross-stitch sparks.

effects.name: Level-up
effects.how: Two dashed embroidered ellipses (gold #e3b24d and red #c3312b) expand from the hero, 16 gold/red stitch sparks fly out in a ring and 4 buttons pop.

effects.name: Dash
effects.how: Two ghosted copies of the hero sprite behind him at 22% / 11% alpha plus soft fluff puffs (warm glow sprites).

effects.name: Damage numbers
effects.how: 3x5-cell stitched digits (white thread with black outline; crits gold #ffd23c with dark red outline), popping 1.4x for the first 15% of life.

ui.summary: HUD pieces are fabric tags: Aida-texture panels with a satin-stitch border (repeating diagonal gradient), a dashed running-stitch line inset 10 px, and a soft drop shadow. Bars are filled with tiled cross-stitch tiles. The timer is an embroidery hoop (wood rings, metal screw clasp, dashed inner stitch line). Title text is filled with a stitch texture via background-clip: text.

motion: Everything moves in whole stitches: actor sprites snap to the 3.2-unit grid, so movement is slightly steppy like a stop-motion sampler.
Hero walk: 3 frames in the sequence 1,0,2,0, frame index = floor(distance / 5 units) & 3; idle = frame 0. Only the legs row changes.

Small enemies: sequence 0,1,0,2 driven by distance walked (floor(anim * 1.6) & 3). Fast spirit: frames cycle at 5 fps regardless of movement and it hovers 1–2 cells up, toggling with sin(t*2.2) > 0.3.
Spawn: 6 steps of progressive stitching (bottom-up with jitter) while a needle darts across; death plays the steps in reverse with fading.
Glows flicker with two summed sines (e.g. 0.22 + 0.07 sin(9t) + 0.05 sin(23t)); gems bob 0.8 units at 3 rad/s; lanterns bob 0.8 at 4 rad/s.
Hurt: hero blinks at 18 Hz during i-frames (alpha 0.45) with a white-flash overlay; enemy hit flash fades over ~0.7 s.
do: Build every sprite from a cell grid of thread codes and render each cell as a real thread X with underside, top ply and sheen.
Keep the Aida hole grid visible everywhere and aligned with the stitch grid (cells start at multiples of 3.2 units).
Outline silhouettes and region borders with backstitch segments that stop just short of each hole.
Use embroidery vocabulary for every effect: French knots, beads, buttons, sequins, satin stitch, running stitch, loose threads, needles.
Leave lots of bare fabric; use density (dithered sparse stitches) rather than colour to suggest meadow and transitions.
Bake stitch sprites (3 variants per colour) and ground chunks once; fill big areas with seamless stitch patterns.
dont: Don't draw flat filled rectangles or smooth vector shapes for characters – it instantly reads as pixel art, not embroidery.
Don't rotate, scale or sub-cell-offset stitched motifs (projectiles and round sprites like beads are the only rotating things).
Don't use black or grey shadows, hard outlines in vector ink, or neon/saturated digital colours.
Don't stitch the whole ground densely – a solid carpet of stitches hides the fabric and kills the handmade feel.
Don't fade enemies out on death; they unravel stitch by stitch and leave threads.
Don't use more than 3–4 threads per material ramp or invent intermediate colours.
performance: All stitch variants (3 per colour), characters (3 frames x 2 directions + flash + 5 partial spawn masks), props, knots, beads and glows are baked at init. Ground chunks (256 units = 80x80 cells) are built incrementally with a generator: cells are merged into per-colour row runs and filled with one seamless 4x4-stitch pattern each, so a chunk needs ~a dozen fills instead of thousands of drawImage calls. Per frame only sprite blits plus a few additive glows are drawn – cheap even with hundreds of enemies. Hot spots: ground chunk building (noise per cell) and the blur filter used for motif shadows (only at bake time).
